title: A weakly admissible ring together with a weak ideal of definition is a henselian pair
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for a weakly admissible topological ring and a weak ideal of definition, the pair consisting of the ring and that ideal is henselian (statement lines 1115-1120). The proof uses the criterion for henselian pairs: given an etale algebra over the ring and a map from it to the quotient by the ideal, it suffices to lift that map to the ring (proof lines 1122-1126). Because the ring is complete, it in turn suffices to lift the map uniquely modulo every open ideal contained in the chosen one, and since the chosen ideal is a weak ideal of definition the quotient of the ideal by such an open ideal is locally nilpotent, so the lifting statement for locally nilpotent ideals applies (proof lines 1126-1131). The claim is H2: two reductions are chained -- from henselianity to a lifting statement, and from lifting modulo the ideal to lifting modulo each open subideal -- and each is displayed with the criterion it uses.
